question: Can role_host.py host a Pi role the way it hosts Claude and Codex roles (launch under a known id, observe, deliver to the same session, retire), and can a per-launch OpenAI service tier be sent and its applied value observed?

versions.extension: skills/manual-orchestration/scripts/pi_service_tier.ts, revision before the not_requested refactor; the integration tests below ran the committed revision

n: 1 per cell; one machine; a local fake OpenAI Responses endpoint, never a provider
isolation: env -i with HOME and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR in the evidence directory, models.json pointing provider openai at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1, OPENAI_API_KEY a fake value, PI_OFFLINE=1, PI_TELEMETRY=0. No real credential was inherited and no provider was contacted. The openai-codex (subscription) lane was not exercised: the owner reported its quota at 0% and said not to use it.
method: tests/role_host_fakes/fake_openai_responses.py served /v1/responses as SSE and logged each request body. Turn 1: prompt on stdin, `pi --mode json --session-id <uuid4> --name probe-one --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol --thinking low -e pi_service_tier.ts` with tier priority. Turn 2: same --session-id, fake reports tier default. Turn 3: fake delays 30 s; SIGTERM to the process group after 4 s. Turn 4: -e names a missing file.

facts.fact: --session-id with a new uuid4 creates a session under exactly that id; the first stdout record is {type: session, id: <uuid>}; stderr warns that a new session was created.
Piped stdin with no message argument becomes the prompt.
--mode json without -p runs once, ends with agent_settled {aborted: false} and exits 0.

The same --session-id on an existing session continues the same session file with the same header id; the request carried the earlier turn (input items 4 -> 7). One session file exists after both turns.

A .ts extension given with -e loads; the payload returned by before_provider_request reaches the wire (service_tier: priority in the request body); provider_stream_event delivers response.completed with response.service_tier.
When the response reports a tier other than the requested one, the observed record shows the reported tier (requested priority, reported default).

Pi's recorded cost follows the reported tier: 1000 input tokens cost 0.004 with priority reported and 0.002 with default reported (Pi's 2x priority multiplier, openai-responses.js getServiceTierCostMultiplier). Whether that matches OpenAI's price for this model is not established.
AGENTS.md in the working directory reaches the request.
--thinking low is carried in configuration_update input items while reasoning.effort is sent as medium (openai-responses.js CONFIGURATION_UPDATE_REQUEST_EFFORT).
facts.evidence: requests.jsonl n=1 reasoning, n=2 input item types

facts.fact: SIGTERM to the turn's process group ends Pi within 2 s; the session keeps the user message with no assistant reply; no Pi process remained.
A missing -e path exits 1 before any stdout record and creates no session file.

source_facts: pi auth check --provider P --json --no-refresh reports {status, provider, authType} without refreshing or printing the credential (dist/cli/auth-check.js); authType is the stored credential type.
Pi reports an exception thrown by a before_provider_request handler and sends the request unchanged (dist/core/extensions/runner.js emitBeforeProviderRequest).
Pi's bash tool exports PI_SESSION_ID, PI_SESSION_FILE, PI_PROVIDER, PI_MODEL and PI_REASONING_LEVEL to commands by default (dist/core/tools/bash.js).
Pi starts bash-tool commands detached and kills their process trees with SIGKILL when it receives SIGTERM or SIGHUP (dist/utils/shell.js).
A non-sk- OPENAI_API_KEY sent to api.openai.com is treated as a Sign in with ChatGPT token (ai/dist/api/openai-responses.js isChatGPTSignIn).
No coding-agent setting passes serviceTier to the provider; only the payload hook can (grep of coding-agent/dist).
not_established: Any real provider's acceptance or billing of a service tier.
The subscription (openai-codex OAuth) lane end to end.
Whether compaction or branch-summary requests pass through before_provider_request and so carry the tier.
design_consequences: role_host hosts each Pi turn as a detached `pi --mode json --session-id <uuid>` process and verifies the header id (P1, P4).
Turn outcome is read from events, not the exit status (P3; docs/cli-integration.md: JSON mode exits 0 on a failed response).
The tier is per launch through pi_service_tier.ts and reported as requested, injected and observed (P5, P6), because a throwing hook would send the request without it.
retire --force sends SIGTERM only (P10 and the shell.js source fact).
Pi's identity variables join role_host's CALLER_IDENTITY, and whoami reads PI_SESSION_ID.
regression_tests: skills/manual-orchestration/tests/test_role_host_pi.py (RealPiTests drive the installed pi through role_host against the same fake endpoint)
